description: Creates an edited or extended image given one or more source images and a prompt. This endpoint supports GPT Image models.

json_with_file_id.summary: JSON request with uploaded file id

value.prompt: Replace the background with a snowy mountain scene
Add a watercolor effect to this image
Add a watercolor effect to this image

400.description: Invalid image request, including invalid parameters or input.

403.description: The project does not have access to the requested model.

410.description: The requested DALL-E image endpoint is unavailable because it has been retired.

500.description: The image could not be generated or processed.

EditImageBodyJsonParam.description:
JSON request body for image edits.

Use `images` (array of `ImageRefParam`) instead of multipart `image` uploads.
You can reference images via external URLs, data URLs, or uploaded file IDs.
JSON edits support GPT image models.

background.description: Set the background of the generated image output. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their `2026-09-08` snapshots, support `opaque` and `transparent` backgrounds. Transparent backgrounds are available for supported GPT Image models. For `gpt-image-2` and `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, this support is in preview. When using `transparent`, set the output format to `png` or `webp`.

images.description:
Input image references to edit.
For GPT image models, you can provide up to 16 images.

input_fidelity.description: Control how much effort the model will exert to match the style and features, especially facial features, of input images. Supports `high` and `low` on `gpt-image-1.5`; `gpt-image-1-mini` supports only `low`. For `gpt-image-2`, omit this parameter. Defaults to `low` on supported models.

markup.description: A transparent PNG overlaid on the first image, referenced by file ID, HTTPS URL, or base64 data URL. Must match that image's dimensions after orientation and contain transparent pixels. Supports GPT Image 2.5. Cannot be combined with mask.

model.description:
The GPT image model to use for image editing, including `gpt-image-2`, its dated
snapshot `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,
`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`,
`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, and `gpt-image-2.6-flare`.
Defaults to `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`.

`gpt-image-1` was shut down on October 23, 2026. Use
`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare` instead.

moderation.description: Moderation level for GPT image models.

n.description: The number of edited images to generate.

output_format.description: Output image format. Supported for GPT image models. SVG output requires a supported image model and project access.

prompt.description: A text description of the desired image edit.
prompt.example: Add a watercolor effect and keep the subject centered

quality.description:
Output quality for GPT image models. The GPT image models support `low`, `medium`,
and `high`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their
`2026-09-08` snapshots, also support `xhigh` and `max`. Defaults to `auto`.

safety_identifier.description: A stable identifier for an end user in your organization, used for safety monitoring and abuse detection. Hash a username or email address to avoid sending identifying information. A non-empty value takes precedence over the deprecated `user` parameter. If omitted, null, or empty, the API uses `user` when available. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).

size.description: The size of the generated images. For `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, arbitrary resolutions are supported as `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings, for example `1536x864`. Width and height must both be divisible by 16 and the requested aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Resolutions above `2560x1440` are experimental, and the maximum supported resolution is `3840x2160`. The requested size must also satisfy the model's current pixel and edge limits. The standard sizes `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, and `1024x1536` are supported by the GPT image models; `auto` is supported for models that allow automatic sizing.

stream.description: Stream partial image results as events.

svg.description: Selects the author model and reasoning effort for `output_format=svg`. Supply `svg.model` when SVG model selection is enabled. Otherwise, omit this object. SVG output requires `n=1` and cannot use streaming, partial images, or output compression.

user.description: Deprecated: use `safety_identifier` instead. This parameter remains accepted for backward compatibility and is used when `safety_identifier` is omitted, null, or empty. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).

background.description:
Set the background of the generated image(s). This parameter is only supported for
the GPT image models. Must be one of `transparent`, `opaque`, or `auto` (default
value). When `auto` is used, the model will automatically determine the best
background for the image.

`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their `2026-09-08`
snapshots, support `opaque` and `transparent` backgrounds. Transparent backgrounds
are available for supported GPT Image models. For `gpt-image-2` and
`gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, this support is in preview. When using `transparent`,
set the output format to `png` or `webp`.

image.description:
The image(s) to edit. Must be a supported image file or an array of images.

For the GPT image models (`gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`,
`gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,
`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and
`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`), each image should be a `png`, `webp`, or `jpg`
file less than 50MB. You can provide up to 16 images. `chatgpt-image-latest`
follows the same input constraints as GPT image models.

markup.description: A transparent PNG overlaid on the first image to guide the edit. Must match that image's dimensions after orientation and contain transparent pixels. Supports GPT Image 2.5. Cannot be combined with mask.

mask.description: An additional image whose fully transparent areas (e.g. where alpha is zero) indicate where `image` should be edited. If there are multiple images provided, the mask will be applied on the first image. Must be a valid PNG file, less than 4MB, and have the same dimensions as `image`.

model.description:
The GPT image model to use for image editing
(`gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, `gpt-image-2`,
`gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`,
`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`,
`gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.6-flare`,
or `chatgpt-image-latest`).

`gpt-image-1` was shut down on October 23, 2026. Use
`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.5-flare` instead.

n.description: The number of images to generate. Must be between 1 and 10.

output_compression.description:
The compression level (0-100%) for the generated images. This parameter
is only supported for the GPT image models with the `webp` or `jpeg` output
formats, and defaults to 100.

output_format.description:
The format in which the generated images are returned. This parameter is
only supported for the GPT image models.
The default value is `png`.
SVG output requires a supported image model and project access.

prompt.description: A text description of the desired image(s). The maximum length is 32000 characters for the GPT image models.
prompt.example: A cute baby sea otter wearing a beret

quality.description: The quality of the image that will be generated for GPT image models. The GPT image models support `low`, `medium`, and `high`. `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, including their `2026-09-08` snapshots, also support `xhigh` and `max`. Defaults to `auto`.

response_format.description: Legacy response format parameter for retired image models. Unsupported for GPT image models, which always return base64-encoded images.

safety_identifier.description: A stable identifier for an end user in your organization, used for safety monitoring and abuse detection. Hash a username or email address to avoid sending identifying information. A non-empty value takes precedence over the deprecated `user` parameter. If omitted, null, or empty, the API uses `user` when available. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).

size.description: The size of the generated images. Defaults to `auto`. For `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-2026-09-08`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-flare-2026-09-08`, arbitrary resolutions are supported as `WIDTHxHEIGHT` strings, for example `1536x864`. Width and height must both be divisible by 16 and the requested aspect ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1. Resolutions above `2560x1440` are experimental, and the maximum supported resolution is `3840x2160`. The requested size must also satisfy the model's current pixel and edge limits. The standard sizes `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, and `1024x1536` are supported by the GPT image models; `auto` is supported for models that allow automatic sizing.

stream.description:
Edit the image in streaming mode. Defaults to `false`. See the
[Image generation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation) for more information.

svg.description: Selects the author model and reasoning effort for `output_format=svg`. Supply `svg.model` when SVG model selection is enabled. Otherwise, omit this object. SVG output requires `n=1` and cannot use streaming, partial images, or output compression. Use multipart fields such as `svg[model]`.

user.description: Deprecated: use `safety_identifier` instead. This parameter remains accepted for backward compatibility and is used when `safety_identifier` is omitted, null, or empty. [Learn more](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices#implement-safety-identifiers).

ImagesResponse.description: The response from the image generation endpoint.

background.description: The background parameter used for the image generation. Either `transparent` or `opaque`.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the image was created.

output_format.description: The output format of the generated or edited image.

quality.description: The quality of the image generated. One of `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`.

safety_identifier.description: The effective safety identifier used for safety monitoring and abuse detection. This is the non-empty `safety_identifier` from the request, or the deprecated `user` value when `safety_identifier` is omitted, null, or empty.

size.description: The image dimensions as a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` string, for example `1536x864`.

svg_usage.description: Token usage for SVG authoring, separate from image rendering usage.

ImagesResponse.title: Image generation response

complexity.description: Computation spent planning the image, independently of rendering quality. Uses the image model's configured default when omitted. For SVG output, controls the reference image, independently of the SVG author's reasoning.

frame_count.description: Number of frames for GIF output. Accepts integers from 2 through 16. Defaults to 9 when omitted. Only supported with output_format=gif. The requested size must satisfy the selected model's GIF size limits. GIF output does not support streaming, partial images, masks, or custom output compression. Requires access to the GIF preview for the selected model.

frame_duration_ms.description: Requested delay per GIF frame, in milliseconds. Defaults to 200 when omitted. GIF output rounds to the nearest 10 ms and caps the encoded delay at 655,350 ms per frame. Only supported with output_format=gif.

ImageRefParam.description:
Reference an input image by either URL or uploaded file ID.
Provide exactly one of `image_url` or `file_id`.

file_id.description: The File API ID of an uploaded image to use as input.

image_url.description: A fully qualified URL or base64-encoded data URL.

anyOf.description:
The number of partial images to generate. This parameter is used for
streaming responses that return partial images. Value must be between 0 and 3.
When set to 0, the response will be a single image sent in one streaming event.

Note that the final image may be sent before the full number of partial images
are generated if the full image is generated more quickly.
Reasoning effort for SVG authoring. When omitted, uses the author model's default in both Images and Responses.

InputFidelity.description: Control how much effort the model will exert to match the style and features, especially facial features, of input images. Supports `high` and `low` on `gpt-image-1.5`; `gpt-image-1-mini` supports only `low`. For `gpt-image-2`, omit this parameter. Defaults to `low` on supported models.

markup.description: A transparent PNG overlaid on the first image to guide the edit. Must match that image's dimensions after orientation and contain transparent pixels. Supports GPT Image 2.5 and 2.6. Cannot be combined with mask.

Image.description: Represents the content or the URL of an image generated by the OpenAI API.

b64_json.description: The base64-encoded JSON of the generated image. Returned by default for GPT image models, or when `response_format` is set to `b64_json` for models that support that parameter.

revised_prompt.description: The revised prompt used to generate the image, for models that support prompt revision. Not returned by GPT image models.

url.description: The URL of the generated image when `response_format` is set to `url` for models that support that parameter. Unsupported for GPT image models.

ImageGenUsage.description: For `gpt-image-1` only, the token usage information for the image generation.

input_tokens.description: The number of tokens (images and text) in the input prompt.

output_tokens.description: The number of output tokens generated by the model.

total_tokens.description: The total number of tokens (images and text) used for the image generation.

ImageGenUsage.title: Image generation usage

ImageEditPartialImageEvent.description: Emitted when a partial image is available during image editing streaming.

b64_json.description: Base64-encoded partial image data, suitable for rendering as an image.

background.description: The background setting for the requested edited image.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp when the event was created.

output_format.description: The output format for the requested edited image.

quality.description: The quality setting for the requested edited image.

size.description: The image dimensions as a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` string, for example `1536x864`.

type.description: The type of the event. Always `image_edit.partial_image`.

ImageEditCompletedEvent.description: Emitted when image editing has completed and the final image is available.

b64_json.description: Base64-encoded final edited image data, suitable for rendering as an image.

background.description: The background setting for the edited image.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp when the event was created.

output_format.description: The output format for the edited image.

quality.description: The quality setting for the edited image.

safety_identifier.description: The effective safety identifier used for safety monitoring and abuse detection. This is the non-empty `safety_identifier` from the request, or the deprecated `user` value when `safety_identifier` is omitted, null, or empty.

size.description: The image dimensions as a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` string, for example `1536x864`.

type.description: The type of the event. Always `image_edit.completed`.

SvgReasoningParam.description: Reasoning effort for SVG authoring. When omitted, uses the author model's default in both Images and Responses.

oneOf.description: Controls how much effort the model should spend on reasoning for this request.

ImageGenInputUsageDetails.description: The input tokens detailed information for the image generation.

image_tokens.description: The number of image tokens in the input prompt.

text_tokens.description: The number of text tokens in the input prompt.

ImageGenInputUsageDetails.title: Input usage details

ImageGenOutputTokensDetails.description: The output token details for the image generation.

image_tokens.description: The number of image output tokens generated by the model.

text_tokens.description: The number of text output tokens generated by the model.

ImagesUsage.description: For the GPT image models only, the token usage information for the image generation.

input_tokens_details.description: The input tokens detailed information for the image generation.

image_tokens.description: The number of image tokens in the input prompt.

text_tokens.description: The number of text tokens in the input prompt.

output_tokens.description: The number of image tokens in the output image.

detailed_explanation.description: The public explanation for this block.

error_type.description: An optional classification; clients must accept additional values.

anyOf.description: An opaque target for explicitly continuing this review, or null when unavailable.

error.message: Your request rate increased too quickly. Please reduce the request rate and gradually increase it again.

InferenceRateLimited.description: The request was rejected because a rate limit was exceeded. A slow_down error means traffic increased too quickly; reduce your request rate, then increase it gradually.

Retry-After.description: The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted.

serverOverloaded.summary: The requested model is temporarily overloaded

error.message: The model is temporarily overloaded. Please retry your request after a brief delay.

InferenceServiceUnavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. A server_is_overloaded error means the requested model is temporarily overloaded; retry after a brief delay.

Retry-After.description: The minimum number of seconds to wait before retrying. This header is returned when the server has computed a retry delay and may be omitted.
